prompt: Leo reviews vocabulary only when words already feel completely forgotten, cramming them all in one evening each fortnight. Why is this weaker than spaced retrieval?

options.text: Fortnightly study is always too infrequent to learn anything
Reviewing at expanding intervals, while he can still partly recall the word and must retrieve it, strengthens memory more efficiently
Vocabulary can only be learned by writing each word 20 times
He should review every word every day with no gaps at all

explanation: Spaced repetition uses the effort of retrieving a partly-remembered item. Waiting until it is fully forgotten turns review into relearning, and massing it in one evening wastes that spacing benefit.
